questions.questionText: What is the greatest whole number less than the square root of 58?
questions.explanation: 7 squared is 49 and 8 squared is 64. Therefore 7 < sqrt(58) < 8.

questions.questionText: Which pair of consecutive integers encloses the square root of 115?
A square patio has area 38 square meters. Estimate its side length to the nearest tenth of a meter.
questions.explanation: 6.15 squared = 37.8225, so sqrt(38) is above the rounding midpoint 6.15 and below 6.25; it rounds to 6.2.

questions.questionText: A rod has length sqrt(67) meters. Which interval gives a justified bound?
questions.explanation: 8.1 squared = 65.61 and 8.2 squared = 67.24. The area 67 lies between these squares.

questions.questionText: A square tile has area 21 square centimeters. Its side length is sqrt(21). What is the smallest whole-centimeter width of a box that can fit this side?
questions.explanation: 4 squared < 21 < 5 squared. The side is greater than 4, so a whole-centimeter width must be at least 5.

questions.questionText: A student rounds sqrt(30) to 5.4 because 5.4 squared is below 30. Which reasoning corrects the rounding?
questions.correctAnswer: 5.45 squared is 29.7025, so sqrt(30) rounds to 5.5.
options: Always round down when a square is below the target.
5.45 squared is 29.7025, so sqrt(30) rounds to 5.5.
questions.explanation: Use the midpoint between 5.4 and 5.5. Since sqrt(30) exceeds 5.45, round up to 5.5.

questions.questionText: Given 7.2 squared = 51.84 and 7.3 squared = 53.29, can these facts alone decide whether sqrt(52) rounds to 7.2 or 7.3?
questions.correctAnswer: No; also compare 52 with the square of the midpoint 7.25.
options: Yes; always choose the lower bound.
No; also compare 52 with the square of the midpoint 7.25.
Yes; always choose the upper bound.
No; square roots cannot be rounded.
questions.explanation: The bounds locate the root, but the midpoint square determines nearest-tenth rounding. Here 7.25 squared = 52.5625, so the result is 7.2.

questions.questionText: Two square gardens have areas 13 and 29 square meters. A straight path has length equal to the sum of their side lengths. Estimate the path length to the nearest tenth of a meter. Keep extra digits until the final rounding.
questions.explanation: sqrt(13) is about 3.60555 and sqrt(29) about 5.38516. Their sum is about 8.99071, which rounds to 9.0.
